title: Graphing a Shifted Cube Root Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = cbrt(x - 1) - 1 by identifying its parent function, shifts, inflection point, domain, range, and intercepts.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = \sqrt[3]{x} \text{ shifted right } 1 \text{ and down } 1;\quad \text{Inflection point: } (1, -1),\quad \text{Domain: } (-\infty, \infty),\quad \text{Range: } (-\infty, \infty),\quad \text{Intercepts: } (2, 0),\ (0, -2)

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Translations
steps.explanation: The parent function is the cube root graph y = cbrt(x). Replacing x with x - 1 shifts the graph right 1 unit, and subtracting 1 shifts it down 1 unit.
steps.why: In y = f(x - 1) - 1, the translation vector is (1, -1).

steps.title: Determine the Inflection Point, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: Because real cube roots are defined and surjective over all real numbers, both the domain and range are (-infinity, infinity). The point of inflection (with a vertical tangent line) shifts from (0, 0) to (1, -1).
steps.why: Rigid translation preserves the domain R, range R, and vertical-tangent inflection point of y = cbrt(x).

steps.title: Compute the Coordinate Axis Intercepts
steps.explanation: The strictly increasing S-shaped curve passes through (0, -2), its inflection point (1, -1), and (2, 0).
steps.why: Evaluating at x = 0 and solving y = 0 gives the exact axis intercepts.
